# Attribution and license

New work by Ross Richardson (@RossRichardson), with substantial OpenAI Codex
assistance in the mathematical argument, implementation, verification and prose.
Apache-2.0; see the accompanying LICENSE, copied from the repository root.
No independent human or delegated-agent review is claimed.

PR934 by Ross Richardson, pinned at
f3100aec6ce6a7b061987875d5e9a8b93801ac0b, is the concurrent direct predecessor:
binary connector walks, the support bound, explicit recursive lowering and a
careful binary/linear interface boundary. PR889, submitted by @CubeJerry and
pinned at e2021d1c9e06948528cbc0a8fd7079b671da981d, supplies the signed common-
factor fanout contract, star comparators and cost accounting. Both READMEs and
notices are retained byte for byte; no source notice is silently corrected.
No executable code from either contribution is imported.

Concurrent PR938 counts minimum words in the one-source signed fanout model.
PR943 at cf360b4b09b7d0419decdd6ac85421fefed55bdd gives a four/five-source
binary boundary. Both are by Ross Richardson with substantial Codex assistance.
They concern distinct query domains; their results and code are not used to
establish this signed three-source classification.

Chafik Boukhalfa (@chafreaky), PR628 at
0768f97d06c623b8211e651543c66135796b62bf, supplies the dirty product commutator
and literal-inverse convention credited by both predecessors. PR822's connector
borrowing and PR929's grouped cyclic inverse have distinct contracts; their
savings are not combined here. PR677 already resolves the native-query shear
candidate rejected during task selection. The archived Fourier-boundary
diagnostic by Douglas Colkitt is acknowledged; no free address transform is
introduced to evade its assumptions.

The commutator identity, signed linear algebra and exhaustive finite scheduling
are standard methods; no literature-priority claim is made. The contribution
is the signed three-by-three classification, its one-orbit obstruction,
explicit 14-query repair, complete cost recurrence and independent exact checks.

Jeremy Kothe, Chafik Boukhalfa, DreamingOfClouds, eumemic, icekylinx, Rohan Arun
and the cumulative community retain attribution for the selected construction
and its ancestry. Their conditional bound is neither changed nor relabeled as
this contribution. The OpenAI #109 framework and all inherited full-theorem
obligations remain separate.
